note: How fast the robot gets hungry, and how full it can get (pluggybot issue
#36). DATA, not code, on exactly the terms economy/rewards.json and
economy/cadence.json are: this is policy about a world, it wants re-tuning
against MEASURED throughput rather than against intuition, and a deploy has
to be able to change it on a mounted volume without a rebuild --
$PLUGGY_METABOLISM=/path/to/metabolism.json.
Points are FOOD. They are earned by working and consumed by living, and
once the robot has enough it is satisfied and spends its time on its own
goals instead. The whole mechanic is the free time; the numbers below are
what decides whether there is any.
MEASURED, two unattended 1-sim-hour `home` runs, no overseer (issue #36's
calibration comment). What the robot actually BANKS in a sim-hour:
hosting cell (8 Wh)   102 points/hour   6 jobs done, 4 failed, 6 expired
demo cell (1.1 Wh)     80 points/hour   ZERO jobs done -- see the warning
So 45/hour is ~44 % of the hosting world's income, which is issue #36's
'roughly half the robot's capacity is its own'.
THE RHYTHM, measured on a third run (the same hour, with --metabolism on),
which banked 102 and ate 43 -- an independent confirmation of both numbers:
t=   0  starving   0    a cold ledger; a fresh robot has earned nothing
t= 230  fed       20    first census banked
t= 240  hungry    19    ...and a point eaten again -- see the wobble note
t= 875  fed       32
t=2643  satisfied 51    44 minutes in, and the free time starts
t=3601  satisfied 59/90 still satisfied when the mission's clock ran out
⚠ THE CYCLE IS LONGER THAN ONE MISSION, and that is the honest reading
rather than a fault. The idealised arithmetic says ~26 min up and ~33 min
down; the measured climb took 44 min from cold, because real income is
LUMPY -- a 640 s charge, four failed jobs and a stretch of exploring all
happen inside it. So a watcher sees the full work -> satisfied -> free ->
hungry arc across SEVERAL missions, not within one, which is precisely why
hunger lives in the ledger's file and survives a restart. Do not re-tune to
make one mission show a whole cycle: that is tuning for a demo, and it
would have to roughly halve the rate to do it.
⚠ A ONE-POINT WOBBLE AT `hungryAt` IS EXPECTED, BOUNDED, AND NOT WORTH A
FOURTH THRESHOLD. Only the SATISFIED latch is hysteretic; the fed/hungry
line is a plain threshold, so an award landing exactly on it followed by a
point eaten reads as fed -> hungry ten seconds apart. Measured: ONCE in a
sim-hour. The two states mean the same thing to the robot (keep working),
the latch that actually gates behaviour is the hysteretic one, and buying
this off would cost a threshold nobody could calibrate.
⚠ TUNE ON `--pack hosting`, NEVER ON THE DEMO CELL. On the demo cell the
robot earned ALL 80 of its points by CHARGING -- zero jobs completed in a
full hour -- because a charged demo pack holds 0.990 Wh and every target
except whiteboard_a (0.929 Wh) costs more than that: whiteboard_b 1.113,
the garden census 1.141. A rate tuned against that inverts the mechanic,
making charging the food and work optional, which is the exact opposite of
work -> satisfied -> goal-pursuit. Hosting is what the deployment runs and
is the only pack on which the task economy is the income.
⚠ A THIRD OF THE WORK PAYS NOTHING, and the rate has to survive that. Of
11 resolved jobs on the hosting run, 4 failed outright (three of them the
far-whiteboard navigation problem CLAUDE.md documents) and 6 more expired
unclaimed. The 102 above is already net of that, but the VARIANCE is real:
a bad hour with no income takes the robot from satisfiedAt to zero in
almost exactly one hour, so `starving` is a state this world reaches for
real rather than theoretically. That is the mechanic working -- zero is
narrative and locks nothing -- and it is why it must stay that way.
pointsPerHour  points consumed per SIM hour, charged a whole point at a
time (the fraction between carries in the ledger, so a
restart neither wipes hunger nor back-charges it)
cap            the most the balance may hold. Earnings past it are not
banked, and the ledger says how many were refused rather
than dropping them quietly
satisfiedAt    balance at which the robot has had enough and turns to its
own goals
hungryAt       balance at which it goes back to work. LOWER than
satisfiedAt on purpose: the gap is hysteresis, and without
it a robot sitting on the line flips state every point it
eats. The band is also the rhythm's period -- (satisfiedAt
- hungryAt) / pointsPerHour is how long the free time
lasts
A world block overrides the default block key by key, like cadence.json.
There are deliberately NO world blocks yet: the measurement above is home's
and nobody has run the same hour on room_hub, and a per-world number
invented to look thorough is worse than one honest default.
Re-tune whenever rewards.json or cadence.json moves -- both change what an
hour earns -- and re-run the measurement rather than adjusting by feel.
